From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary flags before the mark-up

1. **"FINAL / not to be re-opened" is the Seller's claim only.** Nothing in the materials shows these positions were agreed at principal level. Check with the Wattlebridge principals before conceding anything on that basis. Seller counsel's own cover note also invites a mark-up.
2. **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence.** Some ranges are plausible for a deal with W&I insurance. Here there are several known, quantified risks, and those belong in specific indemnities and price mechanics, not under a general cap.
3. **The Seller Update conflicts with the Disclosure Letter on the key items:**
   - **Bluefen:** The Update says it is "addressed." The Letter (§2) says there is no final consent and the clause 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.
   - **Riverlark:** The Update says it is "addressed." The Letter (§3) says the facility is not repaid and the security is not discharged.
   - **DD-006 incident:** The Update calls it "not expected to be material." The Letter (§6) says scope, access and the notification position are unknown.
   - **Sandbar renewals:** The Update calls them "ordinary course." The Letter (§8) expressly does not say so.
4. **Timing risk on DD-006.** The Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Any 30-day assessment window under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC has likely passed. We need a current status update urgently.

---

## Issue-by-issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), and by cl 9.3/12.8 effectively applied to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general warranty cap, such as 40–50% (AUD 9.6–12m), absent W&I. The cap should apply *only* to general warranty claims. Fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted and counter higher. Consider landing near 20–30% only if W&I is in place and every carve-out below is secured. *Reason: identified exposures (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) could consume a 20% cap on their own.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket (about 1.04%) operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A tipping basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. A lower basket (about 0.5%, AUD 120k), a de minimis of AUD 10–15k, and aggregation of related or series claims. None of these thresholds should apply to fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities or covenant/leakage claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. *Reason: a deductible combined with no aggregation rule lets related losses, such as the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals, escape or be heavily discounted.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, with "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so two full audit cycles post-Completion are covered. Separate, longer periods for tax, fundamentals and indemnities. Delete the blanket default rule.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the default. *Reason: the default silently shortens tax, title and indemnity claims to 18 months.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A cap of 100% of price; a survival period of 6–7 years, or the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) period; no de minimis or basket; and no qualification by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: a defect in title is a failure of the core bargain, and a 20% cap would leave about 80% of the price unprotected.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out disapplying all limitations, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and buyer-knowledge provisions for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. *Reason: this is non-negotiable. Do not rely on the general law (including ACL s 18) overriding contractual exclusions.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (§1.1–1.2). §1.4 and §11 also disclaim any admission or conclusion.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter." No general data-room or public-register disclosure, except searches made by Buyer's advisers on a stated date. Disclosure should not qualify fundamentals, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosures. *Reason: general disclosure plus §1.4 means the Seller can disclose risks without owning them, which empties the warranties.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer's actual, constructive or imputed knowledge does not reduce any claim, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3 and replace it. *Reason: "discoverable" creates constructive knowledge and adds a second, backdoor general disclosure. The Australian position on this point is unsettled, so an express clause is needed.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; the condition is "treated as satisfied on delivery" of written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent that is satisfied only by unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived and no adverse amendment to terms. The CP should be waivable by the Buyer only, with a sunset date and a termination right. The Seller should use best endeavours, and Buyer should have input on approach communications.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the drafting. *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and a consent that carries unsatisfied conditions is not a consent.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price, treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics. Delivery at Completion of a payoff letter, a deed of release, and PPSR and any mortgage releases. A specific indemnity for any break costs or change-of-control default under cl 8.1.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: about AUD 3.2m of secured debt surviving Completion breaches the debt-free baseline and could encumber the shares or assets acquired.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420k are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus all on-costs (PAYG withholding, superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, workers compensation) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt and deducted from the price. They should be paid through Company payroll at or after Completion and backed by a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: the employing Company, which the Buyer will own, bears the liability. Unless itemised, that is about AUD 420k plus on-costs of value leakage (on-cost rates to be confirmed by tax advisers).*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A completion deliverable of evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (the AUD 180k is shown as open, unverified) and a confirmatory IP assignment deed from Ironquay. Also a full IP indemnity covering ownership defects, third-party claims and re-development or licensing costs, outside the cap, with extended survival.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity. *Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 materials does not pass until full payment, so the risk is loss of core IP, not a AUD 180k debt.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** An immediate status update and the forensic findings. A pre-Completion covenant to complete the Part IIIC assessment and make any required OAIC or individual notifications. A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and disclosure, covering regulatory, remediation, notification and third-party losses, with 3+ years' survival. Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation. *Reason: about 1,240 records sent to an unintended recipient with no confirmed scope or access position is an open regulatory exposure, and statutory timing has likely been missed.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k (AUD 110k each) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Documents showing whether each renewal is committed, terminable and accrued, and why it was split three ways. If not ordinary course, treat as leakage or Debt, or secure a specific indemnity. The related-claims aggregation rule from SPA-N-002 also applies here.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept until verified. *Reason: the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (§8) refuses to call them ordinary course, and the split suggests structuring around thresholds.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental warranties, (c) tax warranties and indemnity, (d) specific indemnities, and (e) covenant/leakage/price-adjustment claims. Each category should have its own cap, threshold, time limit and disclosure rule, and categories (b)–(e) should be expressly excluded from the general limitations.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the blanket wording. *Reason: this one drafting rule quietly undoes every carve-out the Buyer negotiates elsewhere.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Its own verification through ASIC searches, the constitution and issue history, checks for options, convertibles or rights, and PPSR searches (Riverlark security may extend to the shares). Completion deliverables of share transfers, certificates, register updates and encumbrance releases, backed by a full fundamental title warranty (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. *Reason: the Seller's own §10 confirms the register is merely the source relied on and not a verification.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of price, surviving at least the applicable ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years). No basket, and no qualification by disclosure.
  - **IP:** Elevated IP warranties with a higher cap and longer survival than general warranties, coordinated with the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and reject "settled." *Reason: nothing in the materials records agreement, and the general regime would cap tax at 20% and cut it off at 18 months.*

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Non-negotiables:** fraud carve-out (005), category separation (014), fundamental/title regime (004, 015).
2. **Money at Completion:** Riverlark repayment (009), bonuses and on-costs in the funds flow (010).
3. **Conditions and specific indemnities:** Bluefen (008), Ironquay (011), DD-006 (012), Sandbar (013), tax (016).
4. **General regime:** disclosure (006), knowledge (007), cap, basket and time limits (001–003).

**Suggested next steps:**
- Confirm with the principals whether anything was in fact agreed.
- Request the current DD-006 status, Bluefen correspondence, the Riverlark payoff figure, Ironquay payment evidence and the Sandbar contracts.
- Ask whether W&I is being pursued, since that affects how hard to push on SPA-N-001 to 003.
- Have NSW counsel and tax advisers confirm statutory periods and on-cost rates before the figures go into the mark-up.

  - **Tax:** A stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, capped at 100% of price, surviving at least the applicable ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years). No basket, and no qualification by disclosure.
  - **IP:** Elevated IP warranties with a higher cap and longer survival than general warranties, coordinated with the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and reject "settled." *Reason: nothing in the materials records agreement, and the general regime would cap tax at 20% and cut it off at 18 months.*
